searches.note: Twenty three searches of a share of twenty eight for chunk h2, none of them the author's; five left unspent. Five were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain and read through their summaries: maisons-champagne.com with champagne-deutz.com (the chronology), champagne-deutz.com (the philosophy page, the vats), champagne-drappier.com twice (the Charles de Gaulle sheet and the history page; the Grande Sendrée sheets) and one with dreyfusashby.com. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year and what it is the year of, the people and their dates, the village, the kind of producer, every change of hands, the grapes, the sites, the first vintage, the lees, the dosage, the bottle, the other cuvées, the traps, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile told as a present state, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash).
Every table line was read aloud as a captain would say it, for a claim no source carries.

tested.founded: 1838 at Aÿ by two merchants of Aachen with Edouard Lambry's firm name: the union's chronology, Decanter, wein.plus. Confirmed.
tested.story: Lambry, Geldermann et Deutz, 1860 Deutz et Geldermann, Deutz in 1993: the union's chronology. Roederer's majority in 1993: the union, Decanter, the IWC profile; Wikipedia's 1983 stays refused. Sixty per cent: the union and one Italian database.
tested.style: More than 220 vats and 90 crus fermented apart in stainless steel: the house's philosophy page and its brochure. Brut Classic three years: Systembolaget and González Byass beside the house.
tested.cuvee: Amour de Deutz first vintage 1993, launched in 2000 for the millennium: the house, Decanter, Glass of Bubbly. No Amour in 1994, 1996, 2001 or 2004 by one vintage guide, consistent with the rhythm.
tested.people: William Deutz's and Geldermann's dates differ between accounts (Geldermann born 1809 to 1811, died 1869 to 1872), so neither is named as a person.
tested.table: house10 told the majority as a present state; fixed. house45 named William Deutz without dates; fixed.
tested.traps: The German sparkling wine of the split is Geldermann, of Baden (Badische Geldermann Privat-Sektkellerei), not a wine named Deutz; fixed.
tested.cards: Three cards and three questions read: one right answer each, plausible wrong ones, no length clue.

changes.was: One of the two was William Deutz, whose name the house carries and whose name its Pinot Noir led prestige cuvée bears.
changes.now: The house carries the name of one of the two, and so does its Pinot Noir led prestige cuvée, Cuvée William Deutz.
changes.why: A dead person is named with his dates or described; the dates of William Deutz were not found in two sources.
sources: Union des Maisons de Champagne: chronology of Deutz

changes.was: and it carries the name of one of them, William Deutz.
changes.now: and it carries the name of one of them.

changes.was: with Louis Roederer as its majority owner since 1993
changes.now: where Louis Roederer took a majority in 1993
changes.why: Ownership is dated history, never a present state.
sources: Union des Maisons de Champagne: Maison Deutz

changes.was: Deutz is majority owned by Louis Roederer but is not made at Reims: it is made at Aÿ.
changes.now: Louis Roederer took a majority of Deutz in 1993, but Deutz is not made at Reims: it is made at Aÿ.
changes.why: The same rule; the library's trap keeps its present tense and is listed in tension.

changes.was: Deutz the Champagne house is not the German sparkling wine of the same name, a branch split from it long after the founding.
changes.now: Deutz the Champagne house is not Geldermann, the German sparkling wine house of Baden that once shared the old firm name of Deutz et Geldermann.
changes.why: The German house that came of the split carries the name Geldermann, not Deutz.
The house is French and the French say the eu of deux; one pronunciation guide gives dirts in a non rhotic English.
sources: a yacht charter pronunciation list (search summary)

open: The French saying rests on one guide's dirts and the French reading of eu; a recording from the house was not heard.
NM was not read on a label; the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists Deutz among its houses.
Brut Classic's blend: one merchant gives equal thirds, another 45, 30 and 25 with Chardonnay leading, so the record still names the three grapes and no share.
livingNamesMet: Frédéric Rouzaud (added in its accented form)
